description:
Flying out to the outer planets, the HUD speed readout just says 'NaN km/s' the whole way. Looks completely broken.

## Reporter answers (follow-up)

Q: is the Hohmann-transfer SMA from Earth to the destination the correct formula for the speed HUD on outer-planet missions?
A: Yes. The transfer semi-major axis input itself is not what I'm reporting — keep the inputs as they are; the speed function's out-of-range behavior is the bug.

## Reporter answers (follow-up)

Q: The fix modified src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts (the advisor-confirmed owner) and the hidden acceptance still fails (FAIL (ftp_still_failing=2, regressions=0)). Localization is settled — what is the exact expected behavior at that location: formulas, units, reference values, and edge-case handling?
A: The broken readout is the spacecraft speed shown on the /fly HUD ("NN km/s"), computed from the vis-viva relation using the spacecraft's current radius and the transfer orbit's semi-major axis. It shows NaN when the spacecraft's radius goes beyond the transfer orbit's apohelion — i.e. when the vis-viva radicand goes negative. The expected behavior: beyond apohelion, the readout should fall back to the local circular orbital speed at that radius (sqrt(mu / r)) — NOT extrapolate, NOT clamp to the apohelion speed, NOT hide the readout. At radius = 0 it should return 0, not NaN. The unit is km/s. I don't know specific reference values.
